newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan zinc demand seen steady on firm car exports.
newsitem.headline: Japan zinc demand seen steady on firm car exports.

text.p: Japan's strong car exports are likely to keep the country's zinc demand steady this year, zinc industry sources and traders said on Thursday.

"The domestic (zinc) market is pretty tight at the moment. Steelmakers are faring well," said a zinc trader at a European house. "Car production looks set for a growth of five to 10 percent (this year)."
Mining industry sources said Japan's zinc demand in the current business year to March 31, 1998 would be around 631,100 tonnes, against 633,900 tonnes the previous year.
The industry had previously forecast demand of 626,100 tonnes this year, having expected the increase in Japan's sales tax to dent demand more seriously.
However strong demand for rust-resistant galvanised steel sheets, mainly used by the automobile industry, has made the industry revise upwards their outlook.
"If the foreign exchange rate remains at around current levels...we can expect a fair amount of (car) exports. Demand will be much better than earlier expected," one trader said.

Another trader added: "Strong car exports are more than offsetting a fall in domestic car sales. We also heard there are quite a lot of exports of rust-resistant galvanised steel sheets to China, helped by the dollar's strength."

Data released by the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association last week showed that the country's vehicle exports jumped 28.8 percent in May to 346.532 units from the same month of 1996, the 12th successive year-on-year increase.

Higher demand from the car industry and housing sector boosted domestic output of steel by 7.6 percent in the second quarter compared with the same period a year earlier, latest Trade Ministry data shows.
The ministry said steel production in the third quarter is expected to remain unchanged from the second quarter's 26.05 million tonnes.
The strong demand from the car sector has already led to zinc imports by Japanese smelters, who process the metal to match automobile industry specifications, traders said.

Some estimated that Japanese smelters' imports comprised some 70 percent of April zinc imports under the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) scheme, which totalled 112,639 tonnes, up from 83,535 tonnes in the same month of 1996.
"We expect Japanese zinc imports to total about 170,000 tonnes this year. This means there's about 50,000 tonnes yet to be imported," said the trader at the European house.
Some traders said Japanese zinc premiums over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices could start rising later this year if the country's demand remains robust.

In spite of Japan's healthy demand, the premium on zinc has remained little changed in recent months at about $40 to $50 per tonne, reflecting aggressive exports by China, which is keen to take advantage of the metal's high price on the LME.
